name: Variance Analysis and Explanation
title: Variance Analysis and Explanation
answer: Variance analysis and explanation is the work of comparing what a business actually did against what it planned, then saying why the two differ. In forecasting and planning it covers the monthly or quarterly review of budget versus actuals, the decomposition of a gap into its drivers, and the written commentary that finance teams circulate to managers. The output is not just a number but a narrative that a reader can act on, which is why the explanation half of the topic carries as much weight as the arithmetic.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Variance analysis and explanation is the work of comparing what a business actually did against what it planned, then saying why the two differ. In forecasting and planning it covers the monthly or quarterly review of budget versus actuals, the decomposition of a gap into its drivers, and the written commentary that finance teams circulate to managers. The output is not just a number but a narrative that a reader can act on, which is why the explanation half of the topic carries as much weight as the arithmetic.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on the general ledger and the planning system of record, whether that is a dedicated budgeting tool or a spreadsheet model that has grown into one. Actuals arrive from the accounting close, budget and forecast versions sit alongside them, and a mapping layer links accounts to the dimensions used for reporting. Increasingly a language model sits on top of that data to draft the first pass of commentary, but the numbers themselves still come from the ledger and the approved plan.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Analysts start by calculating the total gap and splitting it into price, volume, mix, rate and timing effects, using a consistent order of decomposition so that the pieces add back to the whole. They then compare the result against materiality thresholds to decide what deserves comment, and check whether the driver is a one-off or a trend. The explanation is written against the prior forecast and the prior year, and it is reviewed by the controller or finance business partner before it goes out. Where models assist, they retrieve the relevant figures and draft wording that a human edits and signs off.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The main risks are misstatement, where a plausible story is attached to the wrong number, and overconfidence in a model-generated explanation that no one has checked. Provenance matters: each figure in a variance pack should trace back to a source system, a version of the plan, and a named preparer. Access to forecast data is usually restricted, commentary may be price-sensitive, and any AI tool used in the process needs a clear record of what it was given and what it produced. Audit and internal control expectations apply to the explanation just as they do to the underlying ledger.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward continuous variance monitoring rather than a monthly pack, with anomalies flagged as transactions post and commentary drafted automatically for routine lines. That shifts the analyst's time toward the unusual and the judgement-heavy, and it raises the bar on data quality and on the audit trail behind each explanation. Expect tighter integration between planning systems and the close, more standardised driver taxonomies, and growing scrutiny of how AI-drafted commentary is reviewed and retained.
